\textbf{Universe-aware decomposition of context-versus-global differences.} For each tissue and reference, the ratio of precision among the 500 highest-credibility evaluable edges in the context universe to that in the global universe (raw P@500 ratio) is the product of the base-rate ratio and the Enr@500 ratio \eqref{eq:decomp}; 95\% intervals (post hoc) combine independent TF bootstraps of the two universes. Filled markers: Family-HB credibility from the global fit; open markers: from the context fit. Grey bars: central 95\% of the raw ratio under the prevalence-matched null (1{,}000 random sub-universes of the global universe with the context's numbers of evaluable edges and positives, sampled as edges); dashed boxes: the same null sampled as whole TF blocks matched to the context's per-TF sizes (post hoc), which keeps the within-TF dependence. Pooled perturbation, global-fit credibility: immune: raw 1.28 = base rate 2.57 $\times$ enrichment 0.50 [0.30, 0.80]; kidney: raw 0.70 = base rate 1.55 $\times$ enrichment 0.45 [0.26, 0.73]; lung: raw 1.43 = base rate 3.04 $\times$ enrichment 0.47 [0.28, 0.73]. On ENCODE the raw immune ratio is 0.67 although the enrichment ratio is 1.08, because the context base rate is lower (0.24 vs 0.38); the context P@500 (0.41) lies outside the edge-level null distribution (median 0.35, two-sided empirical $p=4.0\times 10^{-3}$, post hoc) and inside the TF-block null distribution (median 0.32, $p=0.21$); the edge-level null ignores the clustering of edges within TFs and is anti-conservative.
